claims.text: An ab initio-informed neural-network potential can replace an EAM potential as the reference in thermodynamic-integration calculations.
The neural-network potential would capture the diverse atomic configurations of an ab initio liquid.
High-temperature multicomponent HEAs exhibit diverse local atomic arrangements, including chemical clustering or short-range order.
Training on high-fidelity ab initio configurations would allow the neural-network reference to represent a wide range of liquid configurations.
The neural-network potential would mediate a smoother free-energy landscape.
First-principles calculations can provide information about high-temperature short-range ordering in a multicomponent HEA.
Incorporating short-range order and atomic-configuration information would make the neural-network reference phase space more closely overlap the target ab initio phase space.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap would reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The neural-network reference would reduce path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's traditional EAM references.
Reducing thermodynamic-integration path mismatch would improve free-energy estimates.
The method is applicable to solid and liquid high-entropy alloys at or near their melting temperatures.
The applicable alloys contain multiple principal elements, typically at least five.
The approach would be most effective for complex multicomponent alloys at high temperatures.
The benefits may be smaller for elemental or binary systems and at temperatures far from melting.
The magnitude of path-mismatch reduction depends on neural-network training-data quality and coverage, alloy composition, and temperature.
The precise quantitative reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is uncertain.
